summary: The old harness calls png_start_read_image after png_read_update_info has initialized row state on both versions. Whether the duplicate-call report prevents row reading depends on an initial error-policy flag whose value is not supplied.
missing_information: The initial PNG_FLAG_APP_ERRORS_WARN value and the error path are needed to determine whether the duplicate call stops row reading.

assessment.necessity_reason: The duplicate call is established, but the supplied evidence does not show whether png_app_error warns or raises an error in this build. A blocked row read therefore cannot be established.

before.requirement: Continue sequential reading of an accepted PNG's rows after png_read_update_info initializes row state.
before.reason: png_read_update_info initializes the row, then the harness calls png_start_read_image, which reports a duplicate call. The initial PNG_FLAG_APP_ERRORS_WARN value determines whether png_app_error warns or calls png_error.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The earlier update call starts row initialization.
Successful row initialization sets the flag tested by png_start_read_image.
The error-policy flag selects warning or error behavior.

after.requirement: Continue sequential reading of an accepted PNG's rows after png_read_update_info initializes row state.
after.reason: The same duplicate-call path remains. The supplied evidence still does not determine whether its report stops the harness before png_read_row.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The earlier update call starts row initialization.
Successful row initialization sets the flag tested by png_start_read_image.
The error-policy flag selects warning or error behavior.

assessment.comparison_reason: Both versions receive the same old harness call sequence and have the same duplicate-call contract. Whether that sequence is a concrete blocker on either side remains unresolved.
missing_information: The before and after initial PNG_FLAG_APP_ERRORS_WARN value in png_create_png_struct (png.c).
The before and after png_error control flow, including the default error handler (pngerror.c).
